The confident joint

Source: R/joint.R
confident_joint.Rd

confident_joint() counts, for every pair of given label i and (estimated) true label j, the examples labelled i that are confident members of class j (Northcutt et al., 2021, Eq. 1 and Algorithm 1). An example is a confident member of class j when its predicted probability for j is at least the threshold of j (see class_thresholds()). When it is a confident member of several classes, the one with the largest predicted probability among them is used. Examples that are confident members of no class are not counted.

With calibrate = TRUE, each row is rescaled so that it sums to the number of examples with that given label (the numerator of Eq. 3). Rows with no confident examples are treated as noise free.

Off-diagonal cells are label errors: examples given label i that look like they belong to class j.

Usage

confident_joint(x, ..., calibrate = TRUE)

Arguments

x

Labels or an object holding labels and predicted probabilities. See Description.

...

Passed to label_inputs(): for example pred_probs when x is a label vector, or truth when x is a data frame.

calibrate

Rescale rows to the observed class counts?

Value

A square matrix with dimension names given (rows) and true (columns). Integer counts when calibrate = FALSE; real-valued calibrated counts otherwise.

References

Northcutt, C., Jiang, L., & Chuang, I. (2021). Confident learning: Estimating uncertainty in dataset labels. Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, 70, 1373–1411. doi:10.1613/jair.1.12125

See also

estimate_joint(), noise_matrices(), num_label_issues()

Examples

sim <- simulate_label_noise(n = 500, seed = 1)
confident_joint(sim, truth = given, calibrate = FALSE)
#>      true
#> given   A  B  C  D
#>     A 106  5  4  7
#>     B   9 77  6  3
#>     C   5  5 58  3
#>     D   4  7  3 32
confident_joint(sim, truth = given)
#>      true
#> given          A          B         C         D
#>     A 170.295082   8.032787  6.426230 11.245902
#>     B  13.547368 115.905263  9.031579  4.515789
#>     C   7.112676   7.112676 82.507042  4.267606
#>     D   5.217391   9.130435  3.913043 41.739130
